claim: Roads are made for movement, not staying
lead: All three streets move people. Malé has the most people stopping (48%), but they wait or shop, and no children play there. Villimalé’s frontage is 75% dull and few people stay. Hulhumalé’s mixed frontage holds 268 children, yet its six lanes keep three quarters of people moving.

measures.note: % of surveyed street length graded D or E (Toolkit 1)

measures.name: People staying at the gates
measures.note: % of all people counted, staying against moving (Toolkit 5)

notes: Most staying (48%) but no children in the street; frontage 80% dull or inactive.
Frontage 75% dull or inactive; only 26 children logged in the street.
Frontage holds at grade C everywhere; by far the most children in the street (268).

caption.text: Each measure scaled to its largest island.

conclusion: Dull frontage goes with empty streets: 0 and 26 children where 75 to 80% of frontage is graded D or E, against 268 at grade C.
